issues.problem: The API is not operational. Giant Bomb says its game, character, company, release, and other wiki APIs are currently unavailable following its separation from Fandom.
issues.suggestion: Set status to "unavailable" or remove the entry until Giant Bomb relaunches the API. See the [official API notice](https://giantbomb.com/api).

issues.problem: This URL now leads to an informational webpage, not a functioning REST API root.
issues.suggestion: Do not publish a base URL until Giant Bomb documents and launches the replacement API.

issues.problem: The old documentation URL no longer provides usable API documentation.
issues.suggestion: Remove this docs URL; the current /api page is only a service-unavailability notice.

issues.problem: The listed authentication mechanisms are presented as currently usable even though the API interface is unavailable; the alternative header forms are not supported by current published documentation.
issues.suggestion: Remove or mark authentication as unavailable pending replacement API documentation.

issues.problem: There is no currently accessible free API tier because the API endpoints are unavailable.
issues.suggestion: Set free_tier to false or null while the service is unavailable.

issues.problem: The historical /api/game endpoint is currently unavailable, so this curl request will not perform the described lookup.
issues.suggestion: Remove the example until a replacement endpoint is published.

issues.problem: The description says Giant Bomb currently provides a REST API for its encyclopedia data, which is no longer true.
issues.suggestion: Describe the API as historically available and currently being rebuilt.

issues.problem: The free beta-key limit is published, not unknown: 100 API calls per hour.
issues.suggestion: Set this to "100 API calls per hour for beta keys; production access requires approval and paid custom pricing." See the [official GIPHY documentation](https://developers.giphy.com/docs/api/).

issues.problem: The claim that rate limits are not published is false. GIPHY publishes a 100-calls-per-hour limit for beta keys.
issues.suggestion: Use "Beta keys: 100 API calls/hour; production limits are assigned through an approved production key."

issues.problem: The response is internally inconsistent: pagination.total_count is 0 while data contains one result.
issues.suggestion: Use a total_count of at least 1 when returning one data item.

issues.problem: The GitHub App installation wording conflates two rules. Non-Enterprise installations start at 5,000 requests/hour and can scale with repositories and users to a maximum of 12,500; installations on GitHub Enterprise Cloud organizations receive 15,000 requests/hour.
issues.suggestion: Replace the installation portion with the separate 5,000-to-12,500 scaling rule and fixed 15,000 Enterprise Cloud rule documented in [GitHub's rate-limit documentation](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/using-the-rest-api/rate-limits-for-the-rest-api).

issues.problem: The entry omits an important GitLab.com restriction: project and group access tokens require Premium or Ultimate, even though personal access tokens remain available on Free.
issues.suggestion: Add that project/group access tokens are Premium or Ultimate features on GitLab.com but are available in all tiers on self-managed GitLab. See the [GitLab authentication documentation](https://docs.gitlab.com/api/rest/authentication/).

issues.problem: The response snippet is not valid JSON because the bare string property marker "..." has no colon or value.
issues.suggestion: Remove the trailing ",\"...\"" or replace it with a valid placeholder property such as "_omitted":true.

issues.problem: Per-second limits are clearly published: the Free plan allows 1 request/second and paid plans allow 10 requests/second.
issues.suggestion: Set this to "Daily quota varies by plan; Free: 100 requests/day and 1 request/second; paid plans: 10 requests/second." See [GNews error-handling documentation](https://docs.gnews.io/error-handling).

issues.problem: Google does not publish a Books API pay-as-you-go overage price or separate paid API plan. Enabling Cloud billing does not by itself establish that Books requests above the quota are billable.
issues.suggestion: Set paid_plans to null and describe the service as quota-limited; direct users to the Cloud Console or Google support for quota changes.

issues.problem: The response snippet is invalid JSON because the top-level object is missing its final closing brace.
issues.suggestion: Append a final "}" after the items array.

issues.problem: The sample response is unrelated to the request: a search for "climate change" is shown returning an Elvis Presley body-identification claim.
issues.suggestion: Use a climate-related ClaimReview response or change the query to terms matching the Elvis claim.

issues.problem: The statement that OAuth and service-account authentication are available only through Vertex AI is false. The Gemini Developer API itself supports OAuth, and its current authorization-key system binds keys to Google Cloud service accounts.
issues.suggestion: State that Gemini Developer API supports API keys and OAuth; distinguish it from Vertex AI without denying OAuth/service-account-backed authentication. See the [official OAuth guide](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/oauth).

issues.problem: The quoted Gemini 2.5 Flash limits are stale and are no longer a dependable public default. Google now directs users to AI Studio for their active project-specific limits.
issues.suggestion: Remove the numeric example and say that model- and project-specific RPM, TPM, and RPD limits are shown in Google AI Studio.

issues.problem: The curl uses gemini-2.0-flash, which was shut down on June 1, 2026, so the example no longer works.
issues.suggestion: Replace the model with a current supported model such as gemini-3.5-flash and verify its generateContent interface. See the [official deprecation schedule](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/deprecations).

issues.problem: Google Maps Platform is a suite without one universal API root. This URL covers legacy-style Maps web-service endpoints such as Geocoding, but newer products use other hosts, such as routes.googleapis.com and places.googleapis.com.
issues.suggestion: Either scope the entry to the legacy Geocoding-style API represented by this base URL or represent the platform as multiple product-specific API roots.

issues.problem: The reference to a free monthly credit is outdated. The $200 monthly credit was replaced on March 1, 2025 by per-SKU monthly free-usage caps.
issues.suggestion: Use "Pay as you go after each SKU's monthly free-usage cap; caps vary by Essentials, Pro, and Enterprise SKU." See the [official pricing-change FAQ](https://developers.google.com/maps/billing-and-pricing/faq).

issues.problem: The claim that limits are not published is false. Google publishes product-specific limits, including 3,000 QPM for Geocoding and Compute Routes, 3,000 EPM for Compute Route Matrix, and other limits for each service.
issues.suggestion: Replace this with product-specific published quotas or direct users to the [Google Maps Platform usage-limit table](https://developers.google.com/maps/faq).

issues.problem: The description's reference to a monthly free credit is outdated.
issues.suggestion: Replace it with per-SKU monthly free-usage caps, which replaced the $200 credit in March 2025.
